author: Shawn Cunningham
program: Carnegie Mellon University and ExecOnline Agentic AI Program
assignment: Final Capstone Project Report and Presentation Section B

report.summary: DragonWings PAP is a working, read-only agent service that estimates additional solar power available over the next {{horizon}} hours. It combines real MySolArk telemetry, deterministic calculations, durable workflow state, retrieved memory, and bounded model roles. The MVP demonstrates integration and inspectable decisions. Its present evidence supports implementation correctness and bounded execution, while forecast accuracy and model quality still require broader evaluation.

pages.heading: Problem and intended user
paragraphs: An operator of a portable solar and battery system needs to decide whether additional electrical load is reasonable. A current power reading cannot establish future availability because solar generation and existing demand change. A fluent language-model answer is insufficient: the answer requires fresh measurements, consistent units, explicit constraints, and a record of how the calculation was produced.

The intended users are DragonWings operators and engineers reviewing optional-load plans. PAP presents an interval profile, supporting evidence, and guidance or a withholding reason. The operator retains responsibility for equipment decisions. The service has no path for commanding an inverter, battery, generator, or connected load.

pages.heading: Goal scope and evaluation criteria
paragraphs: The goal is an explainable {{horizon}}-hour profile of additional power in kW and interval energy in kWh. After an operator requests a run, the workflow autonomously acquires evidence, validates it, calculates availability, selects any needed model interpretation, and publishes or withholds. Outcome evaluation and memory indexing are explicit operator actions.

The smallest working scope uses the latest persisted DW 1.24 MySolArk scrape, synthetic hourly solar factors, constant measured demand, and zero battery-discharge allowance. It provides evaluation guidance, with live equipment capability still unconfigured. Success criteria are correct arithmetic and units, rejection of stale evidence and observed voltage-floor violations, bounded model execution, durable inspection records, and reproducible local browser behavior. Forecast error and the optional third agent are evaluated separately. [R1, R2]

pages.heading: Final architecture and major components
paragraphs: LangGraph coordinates one typed workflow. PostgreSQL stores canonical telemetry, forecasts, outcomes, provenance, and audit records. The official PostgreSQL checkpointer stores workflow references and control state, allowing execution to resume without treating checkpoint data as a second source of operational facts.

T1 and T2 expose two read-only Model Context Protocol tools for telemetry and weather inputs. T3 validates schemas, units, UTC scrape freshness, and the weather horizon. Deterministic Python implements T4 forecasting, T5 availability arithmetic, and T6 constraints. Available power is nonnegative solar surplus, subject to an equipment cap when configured. Energy integrates each interval once.

The routine route can proceed without model generation. Recorded solar overestimation above a demonstration threshold of 0.25 kW triggers selective search. T9 retrieves qualified memory. LangChain create_agent nodes generate and critique structured guidance using the same evidence. Python prunes candidates, controls the search, and retains numerical authority. T7 rechecks freshness and constraints before publishing or withholding. T8 compares later observations with the forecast and stores feedback for subsequent runs. [R2]

pages.heading: Implementation approach
paragraphs: The native command-line service uses Python, FastAPI, LangGraph, LangChain, and PostgreSQL with pgvector. Environment settings select local Ollama, OpenAI, or Claude. Gemma 3 4B supplies the demonstrated local responses; nomic-embed-text supplies 768-dimensional memory vectors. Cosine retrieval considers five candidates and admits at most three after source, model-version, expiry, relevance, and duplicate checks. Similarity scores rank relevance, not probability.

The HTML, CSS, and JavaScript console follows the conversation-and-inspector idea in Agent-with-Subagent, without Gradio. Six tabs expose context, memory, tools, subagents, trace, and health. A linked run restores its evidence and records; readable summaries precede raw details. Small PRs built the vertical slice with terse teaching lessons. Docker and Deep Agents are excluded. [R1, R2, R7, R8]

pages.heading: Design evolution across checkpoints
paragraphs: Each checkpoint added a capability and clarified its authority. The final implementation narrows several early design ambitions so the full workflow can be demonstrated locally. [C1]

rows: Defined an interval availability forecast for operators because a single present-state reading cannot answer a planning question.
Introduced a ReAct-inspired evidence and feedback cycle. The implementation uses explicit graph steps and persistent records for repeatability.
Added searchable validated history and guidance. Retrieval changes context and advice while current measurements and calculations remain authoritative.
Reserved alternative generation for grounded ambiguity. A small beam and explicit stopping rules limit unnecessary model work.
Separated generator and critic roles. The MVP adds an optional interpretation role, disabled by default, for a controlled comparison.
Layered input, numerical, runtime, and publication checks. Failed checks produce visible withholding and an opportunity for human review.

after: Implementation choices include a {{horizon}}-hour horizon, voltage instead of measured SOC, synthetic weather factors, and no battery discharge. LangGraph owns orchestration, MCP owns the bounded source interface, and model nodes interpret evidence. This keeps one functioning system within the capstone's minimal scope.

pages.heading: Safety reliability and human oversight
paragraphs: A scan of {{scan_n}} MySolArk records found {{floor_v}}–{{max_v}} V. The user designated {{floor_v}} V as the fixed battery floor, corresponding to their approximate 30% reserve policy. PAP withholds at or below that reading and never lowers the floor automatically. This is an operating assumption, not a measured SOC conversion or a guarantee of future voltage.

All model roles receive zero tools and schema-checked outputs with evidence citations. Search permits three children per parent, a beam of two, one refinement, and at most eight shared model attempts. Each call has a 45-second limit and no retry. Durable attempt reservations prevent checkpoint recovery from repeating a call. Operators inspect the evidence and request a new validated run when needed. Approval of prose cannot override hard checks. [R1, R2]

pages.heading: Evaluation methods and results
paragraphs: Deterministic model doubles make required tests reproducible. Cloud adapter checks use actual SDKs with simulated HTTP responses; live cloud performance is unmeasured. Separate browser runs exercise actual MySolArk data and Ollama. These evidence classes do not establish an operational success rate.

It shows added cost without an established quality benefit, so the third role defaults off. PR12 recorded a five-call live run that withheld. PR15 recorded a published sunny-fixture run with four real Ollama calls. Both demonstrate bounded, inspectable outcomes, not advice accuracy. [R3–R8]

pages.heading: Limitations and next improvements
paragraphs: Synthetic weather, constant demand, unknown live equipment capability, and the absence of a battery model limit forecast usefulness. Source timestamps represent persisted scrapes rather than verified device measurement times. Free-text advice can still be wrong despite valid schemas and citations. Optional LangSmith summary export is tested with a fake client, with no remote export claimed.

Next work should validate a real weather source and equipment limits, collect held-out forecast outcomes across changing conditions, and run repeated, order-balanced agent comparisons. Operator review should evaluate whether explanations help decisions. Physical control remains outside scope.

pages.heading: Repository and review instructions
paragraphs: Repository: {{repository}}. The README explains setup and use. Core code, migrations, tests, the final architecture, and PR evidence support technical review. After installing the documented native prerequisites, run make bootstrap, PAP_PROFILE=macmini-replay make run for a synthetic source, and make verify for the local gate. Real data requires the authorized local source database. [R1]

slides.title:
DragonWings
Power Availability
Profile Forecaster
slides.subtitle: A bounded agent for additional solar power estimates
slides.plain: Working MVP with inspectable evidence and human oversight
slides.notes: Hello, I am Shawn Cunningham. My capstone is the DragonWings Power Availability Profile Forecaster, or PAP. It helps an operator review how much additional solar power may be available over the next twelve hours. This is a working local agent service with real telemetry, searchable memory, and bounded model roles. The central design decision is to give numerical calculations and validation to ordinary code, while models interpret evidence. I will walk through the six checkpoints, show how they became one application, and distinguish the implementation results from the forecast quality that still needs broader evaluation.

slides.title: The operator's planning question
slides.question: How much extra load might the next 12 hours support?
slides.what: Estimates additional power and energy by interval.
slides.why: A reading taken now does not establish future availability.
slides.caveat: MVP scope: synthetic weather factors, constant demand, zero battery discharge
slides.notes: The first checkpoint started with an operating question, rather than a choice of framework. An operator can see solar production, load, and battery voltage, but those readings alone do not tell them what optional load might be reasonable later. PAP combines those inputs into a twelve-hour profile. Kilowatts describe power during an interval. Kilowatt-hours describe energy over time. For this MVP, I intentionally limited the calculation to additional solar surplus. It uses synthetic hourly solar factors, keeps measured demand constant, and allocates no battery discharge. These choices make the smallest complete workflow testable, but they also mean the output is evaluation guidance. The operator still makes every equipment decision.

slides.title: One workflow connects the components
slides.branch: Only when the route needs interpretation
slides.storage: PostgreSQL stores evidence and results. LangGraph checkpoints store workflow progress.
slides.what: Runs the evidence-to-decision sequence automatically after a request.
slides.why: Every result can be traced to inputs, calculations, and a stopping decision.
slides.notes: Checkpoint two introduced the tool and feedback cycle. In the implemented system, LangGraph owns the workflow. The first two tools are read-only MCP adapters. One reads the persisted MySolArk scrape and one supplies the current synthetic weather scenario. T3 checks their structure, units, timestamps, and freshness. Python then forecasts, calculates solar surplus, and applies constraints. Only after those calculations does the graph assess whether interpretation is needed. Qualified memory and bounded model roles can supply advice, but they cannot rewrite the calculated power. T7 performs another freshness and constraint check before the result is published or withheld. PostgreSQL stores the actual evidence and results. The graph checkpointer stores progress and record references, which allows a run to resume without creating a competing copy of the facts.

slides.title: Memory adds relevant experience
slides.what: Finds relevant past outcomes and operating guidance.
slides.why: The agent can explain caution using evidence from an earlier run.
slides.caveat: Current measurements and numerical constraints stay authoritative
slides.notes: Checkpoint three added searchable external memory. The operator can compare a forecast with a newer reading, then explicitly index qualified outcome records and short guidance documents. The system creates local embeddings and stores them in pgvector alongside the relational data. A query considers five candidates, checks source, version, expiry, relevance, and duplicates, and passes at most three into model context. Think of this as finding a relevant note from a previous job. It is useful context, but it cannot change the current instrument reading. One actual semantic query about protecting the battery ranked reserve guidance first. That demonstrates the mechanism. It is not an estimate of retrieval accuracy, and the cosine score is not a probability.

slides.title: Extra reasoning has a fixed budget
slides.bounds: One refinement. Depth-three submission. Eight shared model attempts maximum.
slides.what: Compares a few explanations when recorded evidence justifies it.
slides.why: Simple cases stay quick, and difficult cases still terminate.
slides.notes: Checkpoint four introduced selective Tree of Thoughts. Routine evidence takes the direct path to the final publication check and needs no model generation. In the current demonstration, recorded mean solar overestimation above zero point two five kilowatts triggers ambiguity. The generator proposes up to three alternatives. Python removes invalid candidates before the critic evaluates the survivors. The controller retains a beam of two and permits only one refinement before final submission. All roles share a maximum of eight model attempts. Every call also has a time and output limit. These limits bound the search and make termination visible. The alternatives concern interpretation, refreshing evidence, or withholding. They do not propose new battery limits or alter the power formula.

slides.title: The third role added cost in one trial
slides.finding: Calculated kW and kWh stayed identical
slides.what: An environment flag enables an additional interpretation role.
slides.why: Its contribution can be compared before accepting added complexity.
slides.caveat: One sequential pair. No demonstrated quality improvement. Third role defaults off.
slides.notes: Checkpoint five separated the generator and critic so that proposing and evaluating guidance have distinct roles. The MVP also has an optional third role that interprets the evidence before search. An environment variable controls that role, and the browser comparison uses the same telemetry and weather snapshot for both modes. In one actual MySolArk and Ollama pair, two roles used four calls and about fifty-three seconds, producing a valid publication. Three roles used six calls and about seventy seconds, producing a withheld result. The calculated power and energy were identical. This is an informative latency observation, but only one sequential pair. Warm-up and model variability could affect the comparison. I have not established that the third role improves quality, so it remains disabled by default. The same bounded contracts can now use OpenAI or Claude through environment settings. Live cloud comparisons remain future evaluation.

slides.title: Validation controls publication
slides.what: Stops publication when required evidence or checks fail.
slides.why: A convincing explanation must not bypass an operating constraint.
slides.caveat: No equipment commands. No prediction or guarantee of future battery voltage.
slides.notes: Checkpoint six made the safety and oversight boundaries explicit. Input checks, numerical checks, bounded model execution, and the final publication gate each have a visible purpose. A scan of six thousand five hundred twenty-seven MySolArk records found a minimum of three hundred five point two volts. I use that fixed floor under the user's operating policy, which associates it with roughly thirty percent reserve. PAP does not measure SOC or derive a voltage-to-SOC curve. It withholds at or below the configured reading and never reduces the floor automatically. It also does not predict future battery voltage. The operator can inspect a withholding reason, resolve the evidence or configuration, and request another validated run. There are no hardware-control tools.

slides.title: Six views explain each decision
slides.what: Makes the working agent inspectable from one local console.
slides.why: A result is easier to debug when its evidence and decisions are visible.
slides.notes: The integrated console brings these checkpoints together. A selected-run link restores the result, evidence, memory, model records, and workflow. Readable summaries come before expandable raw details. Manual memory search has separate results, so it cannot replace a past run’s context. Tools shows source calls and durations. Subagent shows provider, role, validated output, and usage. Trace shows completed nodes, branch decisions, and stopping reasons. Health checks current dependencies separately; cloud key presence is only a configuration check. Long actions show elapsed time and pending requests. The screenshot is a saved sunny-fixture run with four actual Ollama calls. It published an evaluation profile. These views expose evidence and structured decisions, not private model reasoning.

slides.title: Evidence supports the integrated workflow
slides.checkpoint: Final evaluation   Implemented behavior and limits
slides.what: Tests arithmetic, boundaries, persistence, retrieval, and the browser flow.
slides.why: Separates software correctness from forecast and advice quality.
slides.caveat: Required tests use model doubles. Live checks are small demonstrations, not accuracy rates.
slides.notes: Evaluation uses complementary evidence. The required local gate passed forty-four unit and integration tests plus thirteen Chromium Playwright checks. These cover numerical behavior, voltage policy, model boundaries, search budgets, durable execution, retrieval, and the console. Deterministic model doubles and simulated cloud SDK responses keep required tests repeatable. Separate live checks used actual local telemetry and Ollama. One newer sample measured zero point four one zero kilowatts of solar overestimation and zero point zero seven six kilowatts of availability error. These are point-power comparisons, not measured hourly energy. A live run withheld within its budget; the recorded sunny-fixture run published after four actual model calls. The evidence supports integration and tested boundaries. It does not establish forecast accuracy, calibrated confidence, or model quality.

slides.title: Repository and next steps
next: Repeated agent comparisons and operator review
slides.what: A reproducible local MVP with bounded, observable model roles.
slides.why: The next improvements can be measured against an inspectable baseline.
slides.notes: The repository is at github dot com slash roboyak slash PAP dash Agent. Its README explains the native prerequisites, architecture, setup, and usage. Reviewers can use the synthetic replay profile without the private telemetry database. The code, tests, and PR evidence show each teaching increment. The submission folder contains the editable content and scripts that regenerate this presentation and report. The main strength is the integrated boundary between evidence, deterministic calculation, and model advice, with enough visibility to inspect a run. The next work is to validate real weather and equipment capability, evaluate held-out forecast outcomes, and repeat the agent comparison with order balanced across trials. The result is a working foundation for evaluation, with the limits of its current claims stated explicitly.

faculty_questions.question: Why use agents if ordinary code calculates the power?
faculty_questions.answer: The model roles address interpretation and explanation when recorded evidence is ambiguous. Code already handles the routine calculation. Selective search compares supported guidance such as refreshing evidence or withholding, while retrieval supplies relevant context. I have demonstrated that integration, but not yet that it outperforms deterministic guidance. A code-only baseline is essential to the next evaluation.

faculty_questions.question: What is autonomous, and who controls the workflow?
faculty_questions.answer: After an operator requests a run, LangGraph acquires evidence, validates it, calculates a profile, routes any required model work, and reaches publication or withholding. Python controls branch selection and stopping limits. This is task-level autonomy within one run. It has no continuous scheduling, equipment actuation, or automatic outcome-indexing loop. Evaluation and indexing are explicit operator actions.

faculty_questions.question: Why Gemma 3 4B, and why an optional third role?
faculty_questions.answer: Gemma 3 4B was available locally through Ollama and fit the minimal prototype. It was an implementation choice, not a benchmark winner. Environment settings now support OpenAI and Claude with the same bounded contracts; their SDK paths use simulated HTTP tests, with live comparisons still pending. Generator and critic have distinct roles. One real third-role trial increased calls from four to six and latency from about 53 to 70 seconds without an established quality benefit, so that role defaults off.

faculty_questions.question: What can the models access or change?
faculty_questions.answer: The model roles have zero tools. The graph calls two read-only MCP source adapters, and Python passes bounded, validated evidence into the models. They cannot issue SQL, control hardware, or change numerical constraints. pgvector retrieval filters stored guidance and outcomes before injecting up to three records. Retrieved text can still be irrelevant or misleading, so eligibility checks and citations support inspection rather than proving truth.

faculty_questions.question: What do the current results actually establish?
faculty_questions.answer: Forty-four unit and integration tests plus thirteen Chromium checks support the tested calculations, workflow boundaries, persistence, retrieval, and UI. Required tests use model doubles. Separate actual-model runs demonstrate the live path. One outcome sample and one sequential agent pair are too small to establish forecast accuracy or model quality. I would next use held-out outcomes, a code-only guidance baseline, repeated order-balanced model comparisons, and human ratings of factual support and usefulness.

faculty_questions.question: Does the system guarantee the battery stays above its floor?
faculty_questions.answer: No. It withholds additional power at or below the configured observed-voltage floor of 305.2 V and allocates zero battery discharge. That floor is the user's operating assumption associated with approximately 30% reserve. It is not a calibrated SOC conversion, and the system does not predict future voltage. Existing site load and equipment behavior remain outside this advisory service. A real battery model and verified equipment limits would be needed for stronger claims.

faculty_questions.question: How useful is the forecast while weather is synthetic?
faculty_questions.answer: The present forecast is a persistence-based solar-surplus demonstration. Synthetic factors and constant load make the integrated workflow reproducible, while real telemetry tests the source interface and timestamps. They limit operational usefulness. My next forecast work would validate a real weather source, confirm device measurement-time semantics, establish equipment capability, and measure error over changing conditions before expanding the energy model.

faculty_questions.question: What would you change before serving more sites?
faculty_questions.answer: I would first validate the forecast and agent quality on held-out data. Then I would add explicit site configuration and evidence isolation, measure concurrent database and model load, and introduce scheduling or queues only when needed. Each site would retain fixed numerical constraints, provenance, and bounded model work. Those scale features are future work. The current system intentionally proves one local vertical slice with PostgreSQL as the canonical record.

video_summary: This presentation explains how the DragonWings Power Availability Profile Forecaster evolved across six checkpoints into a working local agent system. It shows how read-only telemetry, deterministic calculations, retrieved memory, and bounded model roles produce an inspectable decision, then reviews the measured implementation results and the remaining limits on forecast and advice quality.
